Done. `out/T3/solution.py` passed on its first execution.

**What it does**

- Reads shapes/dtypes from the safetensors *headers* only (no data) to plan, cross-checking the two input shards against `model.safetensors.index.json` and asserting all 114 inputs are float32.
- Selects the cast set by constructing the 112 names explicitly — `model.layers.<i>.<suffix>` for the 7 listed suffixes, `i` in 0..15 derived from the keys — and asserting each exists with the stated shape. No regex, so no chance of hitting `embed_tokens`/`lm_head`.
- Packs greedily in sorted key order up to 268,435,456 bytes; nothing is deleted or renamed.
- Runs the four required checks on the plan **before** writing, then re-opens every written shard and verifies dtypes, shapes, index agreement, per-shard budget, and bit-exact values (`torch.equal` against `ref.to(torch.bfloat16)` for the cast tensors, against the raw tensor otherwise).

**Result** — `out/T3/`, 114 tensors, 112 bfloat16, 2,971,664,384 bytes of tensor data across 10 shards:

| shard | tensors | bytes |
|---|---|---|
| 00001 | 1 (`lm_head.weight`, f32) | 412,090,368 |
| 00002 | 1 (`model.embed_tokens.weight`, f32) | 412,090,368 |
| 00003–00010 | 14 each (2 layers, bf16) | 268,435,456 each |

Two details worth flagging, both recorded in `out/T3/REPORT.md`:

- One layer is exactly 128 MiB in bfloat16, so two layers hit the 256 MiB budget *exactly*. The packer starts a new shard only when the budget would be exceeded, giving 8 full shards; a `>=` comparison would have produced 16 half-full ones. Both readings satisfy "at most 256 MiB", so if the hidden reference splits per layer, that is where the two would diverge.
- Shard naming and packing order are unspecified by the task. I used the HF convention `model-{i:05d}-of-{n:05d}.safetensors` and sorted key order, matching what the input checkpoint and `safe_open().keys()` already use.
